geomsolver has no surface patch, and its splines are cubic B-splines only (any knots, any weights, but degree 3), so neither the degree-15 patch nor its degree-15 edge and iso-curves can be drawn. The construction its cubic patches use here — the block as a face family whose section is the patch's curve across y on the columns' crossings (`nurbs/bezier-dome`) — needs that curve as a spline of the patch's degree, and a curve written as a formula (a traced Bernstein sum) cannot stand in a face family's section: a trace in the station's component is not elaborated (`no such entity` for the station's own plane).

Solvent reads no STEP or other B-rep file (solventc only writes STEP), so the reference cannot be taken in, and a document drawing the boat from scratch — a hull lofted through its stations, the deck well, the wheelhouse with its framed doors and windows, the chimney's taper, the wheel, the lettering and the fillets — to the reference's volume, area and inertia within 2e-5 is out of reach of this implementation: geomsolver has no B-spline surface from a control net to take the reference's free-form faces as measured, so even a faithful redrawing would approximate them.

Solvent has no surface given by a control net (a Bézier or B-spline patch from its 4 × 4 control points) and no solid bounded by faces sewn together: its solids are sets — prisms, revolutions, lofts and sweeps of plane sections, offsets and Booleans of them — and its one free-form surface, a point of a component traced over two formals, bounds no solid. Each patch's curves of constant u happen to be plane cubics, so a patch could only be imitated as a face family whose section's control points are the patch's Bernstein sums written out by hand as laws in the family's parameter — the surface computed in the document rather than given to the kernel as the patch it is.

Solvent has no ellipsoid with three unequal semi-axes that a sweep can carry. Its sets are balls, cylinders, cones and half-spaces (a bound on summed distances from two foci gives only a spheroid), a set body cannot bound a quadratic form in the point's coordinates, and no word scales a solid affinely. The one way to state the ellipsoid, a face family lofting its elliptic sections (`std.shapes.Ellipse` traced at each station), is a solid the sweep refuses: sliding a lofted body is E080, "material fields currently require prisms, revolutions, Boolean bodies or named motions".

the tool here is itself a swept solid, and geomsolver sweeps no swept solid. The worm's thread is a helicoid, which Solvent states only as a sweep: its trapezoidal section carried up a screw about the worm's axis, as a face family over a declared parameter (or a face read at a roll under the screw). Hobbing then moves that body again, `solid({ p | some t in (0deg, 10800deg): p in thread at(under: worm_turn, seen_from: gear_turn) t })`, and a body made by a sweep or a face family, even clipped by a Boolean, is no source for another sweep (E080: "material fields currently require prisms, revolutions, Boolean bodies or named motions"; for a swept body, "nested continuous sweeps are not yet supported"). Nor has Solvent a set for the thread written in its own coordinates (x - theta reduced mod 2 pi), a set body bounding no expression in a point's coordinates.
